body.x: Wearables, Bluetooth earphones, portable mini-appliances and miniature robots leave little internal space for a battery, and the cell often has to take the shape of whatever room the designer has left.
DongGuan APTPES builds batteries to fit that room.

DongGuan APTPES Co., Ltd, a provincial-level high-tech enterprise in Dongguan, Guangdong Province, and led by Sun Yongcheng, is exhibiting custom lithium polymer battery packs at KES 2026. The display includes ultra-small special-shaped modules for wearables, dedicated batteries for Bluetooth audio and power supplies for portable mini-appliances and miniature robots, and the company says it can produce round, L-shaped and curved cells.

The company develops and makes lithium polymer cells and custom packs at a factory with automated assembly lines, and completes battery solution development, structural design, battery management system (BMS) development, prototyping, mass production and safety testing in house. Its engineers, who have more than 10 years of industry experience, tailor a battery's shape, size, capacity and discharge performance to the customer's device, and every pack has protection against overcharge, overdischarge, overcurrent and overtemperature. The company holds UN38.3, MSDS, CE, FCC and RoHS certifications and follows ISO 9001 quality management standards, with UL and UKCA certifications under application. It accepts orders from small sample batches to mass production as an ODM and OEM supplier.

Southeast Asia is APTPES's main overseas market, where it has delivered several custom battery projects in Vietnam, Malaysia and Indonesia. At KES 2026, it aims to connect with Korean consumer electronics brands and smart hardware manufacturers, and in the longer term it targets Europe and North America, where it is also applying for certifications including UL, UKCA and CE-LVD. It is looking for ODM and OEM partnerships with consumer electronics manufacturers, smart hardware design firms and distributors in Korea, Europe and North America.

From the second half of 2026, the company plans to step up buyer development in Korea, Southeast Asia, Europe and North America and to continue R&D on smaller polymer batteries with higher energy density. APTPES cites the cost and long approval cycles of safety certifications in developed markets and limited marketing channels for finding new overseas customers as its main difficulties, and says buyer matching and subsidies for overseas exhibitions would help.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
